We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have a template (733) that does sulfonamide formation from aryl chloride sulfonyl chloride and an aniline? Let's examine template 733: retro_smarts: [O;D1;H0:2]=[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>Cl-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]

So forward reaction: aryl sulfonyl chloride + aniline -> sulfonamide. Retro: break sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride and aniline.

Thus we can disconnect target into two fragments: aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl) and aniline (aryl-NH2). The target has sulfonamide linking two aryl rings: left ring is tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) attached to N of sulfonamide; right ring is phenyl with a side chain (C=C-CO-NH-phenyl-N). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to left tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) and sulfonyl attached to right phenyl (with side chain). Wait structure: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So sulfonamide nitrogen attached to left tolyl (aniline) and sulfonyl attached to right phenyl (aryl sulfonyl). So we can break into left aniline (p-toluidine) and right aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl with side chain). The right aryl sulfonyl chloride includes the side chain (C=C-CO-NH-phenyl-N). That side chain is an amide attached to phenyl with an extra amine (anilide). So we need further disconnections.

We have also amide formation: we can disconnect the amide between carbonyl and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we can break that amide into an acid chloride (or acid) and aniline. The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Actually /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So we can disconnect amide into acryloyl chloride (CH2=CH-COCl) and aniline (para-aminophenyl). But the acryloyl part is attached to the aryl sulfonyl phenyl via the double bond: the phenyl (right) has substituent /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the double bond is attached to the phenyl ring at para position? Actually the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl (right) has a side chain: -CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (para-aminophenyl). So we can break the amide: the carbonyl attached to N of aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we need to generate the acryloyl phenyl (the unsaturated carbonyl attached to the right phenyl). That could be formed via Heck coupling? But maybe we can use a known template for amide formation from acid chloride and amine. Let's search for amide formation template.

Search for functional_groups_formed "amide". Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_formed ["amide"] and maybe also "acyl chloride". Let's try to find a template that forms amide from acid chloride and amine.
